slots.brief: Two spheres of the same material with different radii falling in the same viscous liquid; compare their terminal velocities using the r² scaling (ask for the ratio, no numbers until options).

Provide a P–V diagram of a cycle composed of an isobaric expansion, an isothermal, and a constant-volume leg; ask for the net work done over the full cycle and heat exchanged in one leg using the first law with monatomic Cv.

A particle moves with constant velocity along a straight line off-setting the origin; ask for the magnitude and direction of its angular momentum about a specified fixed point, and whether it changes along the path.
Give a sinusoidal wave equation y(x,t); ask the student to read off amplitude, wavelength, frequency and wave speed, selecting the correct combination.
Classic Atwood machine with two unequal masses over a frictionless pulley; ask for the acceleration and tension symbolically or with simple numbers.
Series LCR circuit with given R, L, C and applied rms voltage at a stated frequency; compute the impedance (or power factor) by direct substitution.

Two thin prisms of different materials and angles combined for no net deviation; set up deviation and dispersion conditions simultaneously to solve for the required prism angles and/or refractive indices.
Circuit diagram with a silicon diode in series with a resistor and a DC source; using a constant forward voltage drop model, find the circuit current and power dissipated in the diode or resistor.
In YDSE, find the intensity (as a fraction of Imax) at a point whose path difference is an odd fraction of λ (e.g. λ/4 or 3λ/4), possibly requiring the position-to-path-difference conversion first.
Two springs first connected in series then in parallel to the same mass; compare the ratio of time periods, or a cut-spring variant where a spring is cut into pieces and the new k is found.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Light of two different wavelengths incident on the same metal; use Einstein's photoelectric equation to relate stopping potentials and find the work function or the maximum KE ratio for the two wavelengths.
Uniformly charged sphere or long straight charged wire; find the electric field at a given outside distance by constructing a Gaussian surface and substituting into Gauss's law.
Describe a combination of 3–4 gates (e.g. NAND–NOR mix) acting on two inputs; the student must reduce the circuit to a single standard gate (XOR, XNOR etc.) or pick the correct truth-table output.

Three collinear charges with the middle one free to move; find where the third charge must be placed (or its sign/magnitude) for the net force on it to be zero — a multi-force balance with distractor sign issues.

Concave/convex mirror with an object and image condition linked by magnification (e.g. image is real, inverted and of given size ratio); solve mirror formula plus magnification equation for focal length and image distance.

A body projected upward from a planet's surface with a given speed; using energy conservation including the exact GMm/r potential, find the maximum height or the escape-speed condition; distractor uses mgh.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slots.brief: Electron (or alpha particle) accelerated through a given potential difference; compute its de Broglie wavelength directly via λ = h/√(2mqV).

slots.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slots.brief: A plane EM wave of given intensity strikes a surface that is perfectly reflecting or absorbing; find the radiation pressure (or force on the surface) — distinguishing the two reflection cases is the key step.

slots.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slots.brief: A regular polygon loop (e.g. hexagon) carrying current; find B at the centre by summing contributions from each side (with the n→∞ circle limit as a check), requiring careful superposition of finite-wire fields.

slots.subtopic: Moment of inertia of point masses
slots.brief: Point masses placed at the corners of a square/rectangle; compute the moment of inertia about a given axis (through centre, along an edge, or a diagonal), possibly comparing rotation about two axes.

Give the trajectory equation y = ax − bx² of a projectile and ask the student to extract the launch speed and angle of projection by matching with the standard form; possibly combine with range or max-height extraction.

slots.subtopic: Mean free path / mean free time
slots.brief: Multiple-statement MCQ on mean free path and mean free time: dependence on number density and molecular diameter, behaviour with temperature at constant pressure vs constant volume — pick the correct combination.
A wire of given resistance is stretched so that its length increases by a factor n (volume constant); find the new resistance using R ∝ L², with the cross-section change handled implicitly.
A temperature has a specific numerical reading that is equal (or in a given ratio) on two non-standard thermometers (e.g. X and Celsius); use the linear relation between scales to find the reading.
Two bodies with given momentum or KE relationship (e.g. same momentum, different masses); use KE = p²/2m to compare their kinetic energies or momenta.
A source moving at constant speed towards then away from a stationary observer; ask for the ratio of the apparent frequencies in the two cases, or include wind/medium effects at high rigour.
A single parallel-plate capacitor with given C and V; direct substitution into U = ½CV² (or ask energy density given plate area and separation).

Provide an intensity pattern diagram of single-slit diffraction with marked minima positions; ask for the slit width from the angular positions of the minima, or compare positions of secondary maxima with the central maximum.
Given atomic masses of a nucleus X(A,Z) and X(A−1,Z) plus a neutron, compute the neutron separation energy from the mass defect — careful with electron masses when using atomic masses.

Two wires of different materials, lengths, and cross-sectional areas supporting the same load (or a composite rod with fixed ends); set up Young's modulus relations for each and solve for the elongation ratio or the required diameter.

A physical quantity (e.g. density, or resistance from V and I measurements) computed from measured quantities with given least-count errors; propagate relative errors to find the percentage error in the result.

An LR circuit connected to a battery with given L, R and emf; find the current at a stated time using the exponential growth equation, or the time at which current reaches a stated fraction of its maximum.

Show a velocity–time graph (multi-segment, including a negative-velocity portion) of a particle; ask for the displacement or distance travelled in the full time interval, or average speed, requiring careful signed areas.

An atom (hydrogen-like) absorbs a photon of given energy; identify which transitions are possible from the ground state and find the level reached or the number of possible emission lines in the resulting de-excitation cascade.
Two satellites orbiting the same (or related) central bodies; use T² ∝ r³ to compare orbital periods or radii, with simple numeric scaling.

High-rigour conceptual MCQ on γ for gas mixtures: a mixture of monatomic and diatomic gases in given molar ratio — determine the effective Cp, Cv and γ of the mixture, or evaluate statements about degrees of freedom.

A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field at an oblique angle; high-rigour MCQ combining pitch (v∥T), radius (v⊥) and time period — e.g. find the pitch-to-radius ratio or the condition for the particle to re-enter at a specific point.

Two cells with different emfs and internal resistances connected in parallel across an external resistor; find the current through the external resistor (and possibly through each cell) using Kirchhoff's rules.

A car (or body) on a level/curved track negotiating a turn at a given speed; find the minimum coefficient of static friction required, or analyse banking with friction — resolving forces along radial and vertical directions.

Ice at 0°C (or below 0°C) mixed with water at a given temperature in a calorimeter; do a multi-step heat balance including latent heat and check whether all ice melts before setting the final equilibrium temperature.
Four statements on adsorption (physical vs chemical, effect of surface area and temperature, Freundlich x/m = kp^1/n with 1/n between 0 and 1); pick the incorrect one.
Combustion/limiting-reagent problem mixing gas volumes and mole counts; find leftover reactant or product moles, difficulty via impure sample or back-titration style bookkeeping.
Given a few transition metal ions, count unpaired electrons using d-orbital filling; identify the ion with a specified number of unpaired electrons.
Graham's law: compare rates or times of effusion of two gases; give ratio of molecular masses and solve for unknown gas identity or time ratio.
Multi-step reaction with given bond enthalpies and/or ΔH of formation; combine via Hess cycles including ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT correction to find an enthalpy.
Standard cell EMF: add two given half-cell reduction potentials with appropriate reversal, compute E°cell; straightforward single-formula number.
Match artificial sweeteners (saccharin, aspartame, sucralose, alitame) with one defining property/use, e.g. which is stable at cooking temperature or which is a peptide derivative.
Given a disaccharide (e.g. maltose/lactose/sucrose), test multiple statements about glycosidic linkage type, reducing nature and hydrolysis products; pick the correct combination.
Give 2–3 complexes of the type [M(AA)_2X_2]; identify which show geometrical (cis/trans) or optical isomerism and count total isomers.
Figure with concentration-vs-time or ln[A] vs time plots for first-order reactions; extract rate constant from slope or compare two reactants' half-lives.
Group species by hybridisation from bond angle/geometry clues; pick the set where all members have the same hybridisation (e.g. include lone-pair species like NH3, H2O, SF4).
Sequence: phenol to benzene via distillation with Zn, then Friedel–Crafts acylation or similar; identify intermediates and final product; may include Williamson or diazonium route for rigor.

slots.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slots.brief: Rank three unsymmetrical alkenes by heat of hydrogenation or Markovnikov addition; ask which alkene gives a specified single product on hydrogenation.
Kohlrausch's law: given limiting molar conductivities of strong electrolytes, assemble Λ°m of a weak electrolyte such as acetic acid by linear combination.
Order given radicals or carbocations by stability, possibly including benzylic/allylic vs alkyl, and pick the correct decreasing-stability sequence.
Arrange given species by bond length or bond order using resonance/MOT logic (e.g. CO, CO2, carbonate, or NO series); choose the correct order with reasoning on bond order.
Mixed mole-concept + solid-state: solid with two ion types occupying different voids in a lattice with defects; derive the formula or % occupation; combine with density-edge-length to be challenging.
Alkyne chain undergoes selective reagent (Hg2+/H2SO4 hydration or Lindlar) then electrophilic substitution; pick the major product structure from a multi-step scheme.
For a set of octahedral complexes with given ligands, determine high-spin vs low-spin configuration, CFSE, and unpaired electrons; compare magnetic moments and identify the most/least paramagnetic.
Conversion sequence from aniline/nitrobenzene to a target dye intermediate via diazotisation-coupling; identify reagents at each step from options.
Evaluate simple thermodynamic statements (e.g. why entropy increases for gas mixing, spontaneous endothermic processes, or significance of Gibbs free energy sign) — spot the correct statement.
Identify hybridisation/shape of xenon fluoride molecule (XeF4/XeF6) or similar hypervalent species using VSEPR; simple counting with lone-pair placement.
Rank three alkyl halides by SN1 reactivity via carbocation stability (include resonance-stabilised allylic); pick correct decreasing order.
Order given carbanions by stability including aromatic cyclopentadienyl anion; test whether student recognises aromaticity-driven stability.
Amino acid statements: zwitterion form, pH dependence of charge, essential vs non-essential, peptide bond formation; pick the correct set via code options.
Figure showing reaction scheme: substituted phenol/ether with positions marked undergoing nitrosation or HI cleavage; identify the major regio-product or cleavage site with explanation.
Simple fact recall on diborane structure (banana bonds, electron-deficient nature) or boron family anomaly; one-liner definition question.
Equilibrium with reversible gas-phase reaction; build ICE table from initial moles and degree of dissociation α to find Kp or equilibrium composition.
Give a keto/aldehyde substrate (e.g. with alpha Hs and without) and ask for the product with a specified reagent: Aldol vs Cannizzaro; pick the correct structure.
Which statements about photochemical smog / ozone depletion (role of NO2, PAN, CFCs, radical chain) are correct; identify the wrong statement.
Give conversion (e.g. phenol to anisole or alcohol to alkene) and choose the correct reagent/conditions from four options; include Williamson vs alkoxide choice.
Given a multi-step reaction sequence (combination of steps), find the overall K by combining, reversing, and scaling individual equilibrium constants; determine K for the net reaction.
Photon energy / Bohr model: compare emitted photons for two transitions or two hydrogen-like species (H vs He+); set up ratio of energies or radii.
Straight fact recall: colour of a specific transition metal ion in solution (e.g. Cu2+, Ti3+, Ni2+) or reason for colour (d–d transition); pick correct pairing.
Hydrolysis products of covalent halides (e.g. PCl5, NCl3, SiCl4) — complete/balance the reaction and pick the correct product set including HCl formation or disproportionation.
Flow/sequence: start with a calcium compound, follow thermal decomposition and water reaction steps; identify the intermediates and final product in the lime–water cycle.
Figure showing energy level diagram (or Bohr orbit picture) for hydrogen-like species; derive the energy/radius ratio for a transition or compute the wavelength of a transition line.
Multi-step: alkyl halide → elimination → addition of HBr (peroxide effect question) → substitution; identify the final product structure after the full sequence.
Give four orders (ionisation enthalpy, electronegativity, electron gain enthalpy, atomic radius across a set of elements); find the incorrectly stated trend.
Multi-step: identify dissociation (van 't Hoff factor) of a given electrolyte/complex, then compute osmotic pressure or boiling point elevation; combine formulas for a numeric answer.
Sentence on a current-affairs style topic containing subject-verb agreement (collective/each-every type) with all parts grammatically correct so the answer is 'No error'.
2-blank sentence on an abstract theme (e.g., moral dilemma or scientific paradox) where the two blanks demand a nuanced word pair, with close distractors differing only in connotation.
Ask for the closest synonym of a high-register literary word (e.g., 'puerile', 'soporific') in isolation, with distractors being near-synonyms that miss the nuance.
Give a common everyday word (e.g., 'scarce', 'hostile') and ask for its antonym; options should be simple, high-frequency words.

5-sentence paragraph on a general-interest topic (e.g., a historical event or scientific discovery) with logical pronoun/chronological chain; fix the first sentence and ask for the correct order of the rest.
1-blank sentence with a clear context clue (contrast signal like 'although' or 'despite'), where the correct word is determined purely by reading the clue; medium-high difficulty distractors.
4 short sentences (PQRS) on a simple, familiar topic (e.g., daily habit or a well-known fact) with an obvious chronological or pronoun link; ask for the correct PQRS order.
Give a simple, commonly used word (e.g., 'generous', 'weary') and ask for its meaning/synonym with four easy options.
Underlined part of a formal sentence has a subtle gerund-after-preposition or parallelism error (e.g., 'with a view to win' type); ask for the best correction among subtle grammatical alternatives.
Sentence about a familiar everyday situation (e.g., weather, travel, or feelings) with one blank; the context clue makes the correct word evident; easy distractors.
Simple sentence with a blank testing a preposition (e.g., 'insist on/for', 'afraid of'); options are common prepositions, one clearly correct.
Simple sentence divided into parts, one containing a basic tense error (e.g., present perfect with a past-time adverb like 'yesterday'); ask which part has the error.
Sentence with a blank requiring an idiomatic phrasal verb (e.g., 'break down', 'call off', 'put off'); context determines the particle, and distractors share the same verb with different particles.
Four word pairs (e.g., doctor-hospital type relations); three share the same relationship type, one differs subtly — ask which pair is wrongly grouped.
Give a long word and four short options; three cannot be fully formed from the word's letters (one letter missing or repeated insufficiently) — ask which cannot be formed.
Two straightforward all/some statements with four conclusion options; only one conclusion definitely follows — basic Venn deduction.
Number pair where the relation involves a hidden operation (e.g., square of digit sum or product of digits); candidate must infer the rule and pick the analogous pair.
Alpha-numeric series combining letters with positional values and numbers following two interleaved rules; one term breaks the pattern — ask which term is wrong.
Simple consistent letter-shift coding shown via one sample word; ask the code for a new word using the same shift.
A pointing puzzle ('he is the son of my grandfather's only son' style) with three-step chain; ask the exact relation of the speaker to the person pointed at.
Definite integral of an odd/function with f(a+x)=f(a−x) symmetry over a symmetric or shifted interval; use property to reduce to a standard integral.
Given a downward/sideways parabola in standard form, ask for the coordinates of the focus or equation of directrix by reading off 4a.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a given point in a given oblique line using the foot-of-perpendicular/reflection formula and identify the resulting point.
Find the range of a rational function y = (linear)/(quadratic) using the discriminant method; difficulty 2 so keep coefficients simple.
In the binomial expansion of a product (x + 1/x^k)^n, find the term independent of x by equating powers via the general term.
Solve a first-order linear DE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) where P(x) is a rational function needing an integrating factor e^(integral); answer y = f(x) + C.
Evaluate a definite integral of a rational function of sin x (and cos x) over [0, π] or [0, π/2] using t = tan(x/2) substitution; answer a clean closed form.
For a 3×3 matrix A with given |A|, evaluate |adj(adj A)| or a combination like |A·adj A| using determinant identities; hard version with |adj A| = |A|^(n−1) twice.
Sum to n terms of a series whose general term splits as f(k) − f(k+1) (e.g. 1/(k(k+2))); ask for the sum in closed form.
Solve an equation of the form a cos x + b sin x = c (converted to single cosine/sine) and give the general solution in terms of n.
Given a condition like a cos θ + b sin θ = c, prove/evaluate a conditional identity relating cos²θ and sin²θ or symmetric combination; hard multi-step.
Given vectors a, b, c with some relations, compute [a b c] or a related box product using standard expansion identities.
Find the equation of the tangent to a curve (implicit or trig) at a given point by differentiating and evaluating the slope.
Two lines given in Cartesian form; test skewness and find the shortest distance between them using the standard formula.
Given a family of curves with two arbitrary constants, form the differential equation by differentiating twice and eliminating the constants.
Find absolute/local extrema of a cubic or rational function on an interval using first/second derivative tests; ask for max value.
Determine the intervals where a function involving e^x times a polynomial (or log-composite) is strictly increasing, solving a derivative-sign inequality; hardest variant with parameter.
Find the condition on k so that both roots of x² + px + k = 0 lie in a given interval (0,1); combine f(0)>0, f(1)>0, discriminant, vertex location.
Find the value of a parameter for which a 3×3 non-homogeneous system has infinitely many solutions by setting Δ = 0 and checking Δx = Δy = Δz = 0.
Evaluate a definite integral like ∫ x·(inverse trig or log) dx over a simple interval using ILATE order by parts.
Sum of an infinite GP where the first term/common ratio must be extracted from a repeating decimal or a given nth-term description; single-formula answer.
Count the number of onto (surjective) functions from a set with m elements to a set with n elements using inclusion–exclusion formula n!·S(m,n).
Given three position vectors or points, check collinearity by cross product / section formula and find the missing scalar ratio; easy single-step.
Count arrangements of letters/digits of a word or 5-digit numbers where two particular objects must always (or never) sit together; case-wise on adjacent pairs.
Simplify a compound expression like sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y (with a condition on x, y) into a single inverse trig function using standard identities.
Show/verify which of the statement forms (~(p∧q)) → r, (p→r)∨(q→r) etc. are logically equivalent by truth table or algebraic manipulation; pick the equivalent pair.
Find the area enclosed between a parabola and a line (or a line and a circle) with clean intersection points; hard 4/5 variant with two intersection points needing splitting.
Evaluate |z| for z given as a product/quotient of complex numbers, using |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂| and 1/z = z̄/|z|²; simple numbers.
Given an ellipse with centre at a non-origin point (or shifted axes), use sum-of-focal-distances = 2a and distance data to find a, b, and then eccentricity/equation; multi-step 4/5.
Find the equation of a circle through three given points by solving for centre (perpendicular bisectors) or general-form coefficients.
Count the number of ways to select r objects from n distinct types with at least one of a kind excluded, or a committee with simple restrictions; easy case count.
Classic Bayes setup: three machines/bags produce items with different defect rates; given a drawn item is defective, find the probability it came from a specific source.
Find the value(s) of constants a, b making a piecewise function continuous at the joints; hard 4/5 version where differentiability may also be invoked.
Straightforward indefinite/definite integral reducible by a single substitution (t = inner function); easy 2/5 with clean derivative present.
Use the inclusion–exclusion principle on a survey/venn-type data set to find |A∩B∩C| or |exactly two sets|.
Interpret |z − z₁| = k|z − z₂| as an Apollonius circle or use conjugate/locus conditions to find a locus; 4/5 multi-step with modulus property.
Given A² = αA + βI (or A = column×row form), compute Aⁿ and evaluate a specific entry or trace; 4/5 with multi-step reduction.
Very easy: find the domain of √(linear) or 1/(quadratic) by requiring the radicand ≥ 0 or denominator ≠ 0; interval answer.
Given mean and variance of a data set, find the mean and variance/SD after the transformation yᵢ = axᵢ + b; property-based, easy.
Given a binomial situation with P(X = r) related to P(X = r+1) by a ratio, recover n or p, then compute another probability; 4/5.
Probability of drawing cards/balls with at least one condition satisfied; use total minus invalid or direct counting of favourable outcomes.
A line makes angles α, β, γ with axes; given two angles/relations, find the third angle or verify l² + m² + n² = 1 application.
Given two 3D lines with a parameter, find the value of the parameter for which they intersect (or check coplanarity via determinant = 0).
Evaluate a limit of the form (1 − cos kx)/x² or sin(ax)/tan(bx) as x → 0 using standard limits; moderate 3/5.
Find the equation of the line through the intersection of two given lines and a given point (or perpendicular to a given line), using the family L₁ + λL₂ = 0.
